question.problem: Using the standard form of the Maclaurin series of $\frac{1}{1-x},$ find the first three non-zero terms of the series expansion of the definite integral ${\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{4}{4-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.$
question.worked_solution:
Note that

$$
\frac{4}{4-{x}^{2}}=\frac{1}{(1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4})}.
$$

The power series expansion of $\frac{1}{1-x}$ is given by 

$$
\frac{1}{1-x}=1+x+{x}^{2}+⋯.
$$

Replacing $x$ with $\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}$ in the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{(1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4})} & =1+\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{16}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{4}{4-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(1+\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{16}+⋯)\text{d}x \\  & =(x+\frac{{x}^{3}}{12}+\frac{{x}^{5}}{80}+⋯){|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =1+\frac{1}{12}+\frac{1}{80}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$
